traversal_accounting.definition: For token t and edge e in a tree, N_t(e) is the number of traversals in a legal schedule, chi_t(e)=1 iff e lies on the unique original source-destination path P_t, and b_t(e)=(N_t(e)-chi_t(e))/2.
traversal_accounting.identity: N_t(e)=chi_t(e)+2*b_t(e), with b_t(e) a unique nonnegative integer
traversal_accounting.edge_identity: sum_t b_t(e)=s(e)-r(e), where s(e) is the number of swaps on e and r(e)=C(e)/2
traversal_accounting.reason: Each traversal toggles the component of T-e containing the token, so N_t(e) mod 2 equals chi_t(e). Every swap contributes exactly two token traversals on e, and bijective destinations balance the cut so C(e)=2r(e).
traversal_accounting.correction: A swap is not mandatory just because its edge belongs to both original token paths; extra status is counted per token traversal and wrong-direction/repeated traversals contribute to b.

fixed_pairing_dag.equivalence: There exists an opposite-direction pairing at every edge with acyclic token-event precedence graph iff there exists a sequential schedule using exactly half the total initial token distance L/2 swaps.
fixed_pairing_dag.known_boundary: Miltzow et al. (ESA 2016, Lemma 2) prove the L/2 lower bound; Bonnet, Miltzow, and Rzążewski (Algorithmica 2018, Proposition 2) state equality iff a happy-swap-only solution exists. The DAG encodes identity-level precedence constraints of a chosen happy-swap pairing.
fixed_pairing_dag.scope: Sequential swap count only; it does not give a matching-round makespan bound or cover schedules requiring shoves/detours.
fixed_pairing_dag.novelty: No novelty claim; fixed-pairing DAG criterion is a representation of known distance-optimality.

caterpillar_augmentation.target: A polynomial-time matching schedule with R<=c*(D+W_max) for a universal constant c on every caterpillar.
caterpillar_augmentation.status: unresolved; this DAG-augmentation route is closed for now
established_bounds: sum_{e incident to v}s(e)=W(v)+sum_{e incident to v}sum_t b_t(e)
caterpillar_augmentation.missing_obligation: Construct polynomially many realizable token-labeled extra traversals and a matching-round schedule whose resource contention and precedence-chain depth are both O(D+W_max), or prove a schedule-independent parameterized obstruction.
caterpillar_augmentation.no_overclaim: No constant-bound algorithm, asymptotic separation, or experimental result is claimed.

prior_art.citation: Miltzow et al., Approximation and Hardness for Token Swapping, ESA 2016, Lemma 2
prior_art.relevance: Proves the distance-sum L/2 lower bound.

prior_art.citation: Bonnet, Miltzow, and Rzążewski, Complexity of Token Swapping and Its Variants, Algorithmica 80 (2018), Proposition 2
prior_art.relevance: States the exact criterion: optimum equals L/2 iff there is a solution using happy swaps only.

prior_art.citation: Biniaz et al., Token Swapping on Trees, DMTCS 2022
prior_art.relevance: Reviews Akers-Krishnamurthy's happy-swap/shove method and documents that optimal solutions may move correctly placed leaves; relevant to limits of monotone routing.

prior_art.citation: Akers and Krishnamurthy, A Group-Theoretic Model for Symmetric Interconnection Networks, IEEE Transactions on Computers 38(4), 1989
prior_art.relevance: Classical group-theoretic routing source; Biniaz et al. identify its tree happy-swap/shove method. This is not the parallel matching-round makespan objective.

prior_art.citation: Kawahara et al., The Time Complexity of Permutation Routing via Matching, Token Swapping and a Variant, JGAA 2019
prior_art.relevance: Polynomial optimal sequential algorithm for star-path graphs; its matching-round approximation theorem is stated for paths, not the star-path subclass.

prior_art.citation: Bansal, Günlük, and Shapley, Parallel Token Swapping for Qubit Routing, arXiv:2411.18581v2 (2025), Theorem 3
prior_art.relevance: Gives R<=4OPT+min{OPT,h}+1 for subdivided stars (trees with exactly one vertex of degree greater than two); star-path graphs are a special case, so generic star-path matching-round approximation is already covered.
